title: Finite Q3 split Gibbs/KMS source-uniformity stress
question: When the source site of the local q/p-character pair is moved through every site of the finite path4/path6 Q3 graphs, do the Gibbs stationarity and analytic KMS residuals retain the finite mesh-decrease pattern for both split orders, signs and beta values?
method: Reconstruct the registered d=3 Q3 onsite quartic and nonlinear bond matrices on path4 and path6 with chi=1, r=-1, g=3/5, c=3/5 and lambda=1/10.
At every declared source site, use A_x=exp(i a q_x/hbar) and B_x=exp(i a p_x/hbar), the exact finite-H Gibbs state at beta=0.25 and 0.5, and the KMS boundary t+i beta hbar with horizon t=0.1.

Evaluate both onsite-then-lexicographic-bonds and reverse-term split products at delta=0.1 and 0.05 for both real-time signs.  Build the complex inverse in reverse factor order and retain the trace-norm Gibbs stationarity defect and scalar KMS residual.
Require exact-H controls below 1e-9, positive finite split witnesses, source coverage and per-source coarse/fine decrease; treat all ratios as finite diagnostics rather than uniform constants.
Run a non-importing independent reconstruction and an integrated verifier that compares all 160 source rows, 80 mesh rows, provenance hashes, Lean R247 and scope firewalls.
finding: Primary 759/759 and independent 757/757 assertions pass over 160 source/order/sign/beta/mesh rows and 10 source sites; the integrated verifier passes 36/36 with Lean R247 PASS. All source rows have finite nonzero stationarity and KMS residuals. Across the full grid the KMS residual ranges from 8.858509182455559e-05 to 0.007892721200547646 and the stationarity defect from 0.0018261413113423613 to 0.010265665577336547. Every source context decreases when delta goes from 0.1 to 0.05; KMS fine/coarse ratios range from 0.4382134378051144 to 0.6176424250777085 and stationarity ratios from 0.49929112008492216 to 0.4993950046196581. Interior sources have a larger finite KMS residual than boundary sources (path4 maximum-source ratio about 3.19), so source dependence is real even though the path4/path6 ranges are close. No source-uniform or thermodynamic theorem follows.
decision_reason: This extends EXP-001170 from one local source to every site and confirms that the finite equilibrium-interface diagnostic is reproducible while exposing boundary/interior source dependence. The result is a QFT-facing stress test for the required source-uniform common-core estimate, not a proof of that estimate. The observed finite mesh trend and near path-shape agreement cannot replace volume-, source-, cutoff- and beta-uniform analytic control.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite d=3 source-wise Q3 KMS diagnostic. It is not a thermodynamic-limit source-uniformity theorem, a common-alpha construction, a mass-gap proof, a continuum result, or a QFT/Clay closure.

qft_interface.closed: Exact finite-H Gibbs controls and source-wise split stationarity/KMS residuals are reproduced for all sites of path4/path6, both orders and signs, beta=0.25/0.5 and both meshes.
qft_interface.open: A source- and volume-uniform analytic rate, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common unbounded core, all-shape exhaustion independence, one common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS quotient, GNS gap, continuum and physical TECT gates remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 finite evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

adversarial_review.check: Every declared site in both finite path graphs is tested; no translation-invariance shortcut is used.
The alpha_t=exp(-iHt/hbar) convention and t+i beta hbar boundary are applied uniformly at every source and both signs.
The inverse of each complex product is constructed with reversed factor order and -z, not by a complex adjoint.
The d=3 fixture is enforced and a positive noncommutation witness is checked for each graph; the commuting d=2 degeneration is excluded.
Boundary/interior variation is reported explicitly; finite all-site coverage is not promoted to a source-uniform limiting bound.
Per-source coarse/fine decreases are checked on two deltas only and are not promoted to an analytic Trotter rate.
Path4/path6 is a structured finite pair; close residual ranges do not establish arbitrary-shape exhaustion independence.
The independent lane rebuilds matrices and residuals without importing the primary; maximum row discrepancy is approximately 1.3e-13.
R247 checks exact rational finite Gibbs normalization/commutation and conditional-transfer scope; dense source-wise matrices and limits remain Python/open analysis.
Common core, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Use the source variation as a concrete target for a source-uniform weighted common-core estimate; if its constants grow with boundary distance, volume or cutoff, record that route-local obstruction before common-alpha promotion.
no_overclaim: This package proves only finite d=3 matrix identities and diagnostics. It does not prove a source-uniform thermodynamic dynamics, common alpha, OS/KMS identification, a mass gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
